title: New Joiner Immersion Cookbook + Evidence Log
content:
Purpose:
This doc combines a repeatable hiring continuity protocol, a role-specific interview evidence log, and a pragmatic 0-30-90 immersion cookbook for product & infra hires joining distributed teams. Goal: reduce time-to-impact, keep candidate evaluation consistent, and capture interview evidence that maps directly to first-quarter objectives.

Scope:
- Intended audience: hiring managers, interviewers, people ops, and assigned mentors.
- Roles covered: Product, Serving Runtime Eng, SRE, Developer Experience.
- Not a replacement for the full New Hire Handbook; this is a lightweight operational playbook for fast hires and cross-team transfers.

Snapshot hiring plan (high level):
- Role: Senior Serving Runtime Engineer (IC4)
- Req owner: Maya Chen
- Target open -> offer: 6 weeks (expedited pipeline)
- Interview loop: Recruiter screen -> Hiring manager -> 2x technical interviews (system design + debugging) -> 1x cross-team collaboration interview -> final hiring packet review
- Offer approver path: Hiring manager -> Eng Dir -> People Ops -> Legal (if requested)

Interview evidence log (how to capture consistent signals):
- For each interviewer, append a single line per candidate in the shared table with: date, interviewer, role area, question focus, direct quote(s), score 1-5, must-pivot flags ("clarify architecture", "follow-up on latency tradeoffs"), and recommended next steps.
- Minimal example row: 2025-02-20 | Liam O'Connor | Serving Runtime | KV cache design tradeoffs | "Would shard per-tenant cache to avoid thundering" | 4 | follow-up: ask about cold-start mitigations | recommended: proceed to cross-team.

Interview rubric (standardized):
- Scoring: 1 (weak) - 5 (exceptional).
- Competency buckets (each scored independently):
  - System Design & Architecture (design tradeoffs, scaling, reliability)
  - Debugging & Problem Solving (practical triage, root cause thinking)
  - Code Quality & Readability (real examples from take-home or live coding)
  - Collaboration & Communication (ask clarifying Qs, gives concise explanations)
  - Domain Fit (inference infra, GPU/serving knowledge where applicable)
- Pass threshold: median >= 4 and no bucket <= 2. Hiring manager discretion for borderline signals.

Behavioral sample prompts (use as anchors, not scripts):
- Tell us about a time you made a tradeoff to reduce 95th percentile latency. What did you measure? What changed?
- Walk through a postmortem you wrote: how did you assign blame, what safeguards were put in place, how did you communicate to stakeholders?

Evidence-to-onboarding mapping (how interview notes feed 30d plan):
- If candidate showed deep cache experience -> Day 0-14: assign small cache-eviction-focused pairing task with mentor, include code review loop.
- If candidate weaker on collaboration -> explicit syncs: weekly triage rotation + shadow pairing for first 2 sprints.

0-30-90 Immersion Cookbook (practical checklist)
Pre-Start (People Ops / Hiring manager)
- Create account provisioning ticket (cloud, git, internal tools) - JIRA: CLOUD-####
- Shared welcome note to team + Slack intro in #eng-oncall and #serving-runtime
- Assign primary mentor and 2nd reviewer (cross-team)
- Add candidate interview evidence summary to the new hire packet
- Confirm first-week calendar (2x pairing blocks, 1x product intro, 1x infra architecture review)

Day 0 (first day)
- Welcome + high-level orientation (30m): culture, security, SLAs, where to find docs
- Team sync (30m): intro to sprint, current priorities, key contacts
- Setup time (1-2h): local dev env, access checks, perf test scripts
- Short task assigned: run an example end-to-end micro-benchmark and submit run notes to PR

Week 1 (Days 1-7)
- Pairing sessions with primary mentor (3 x 90m) focused on codebase walk-through and creating a low-risk change
- First small PR: fix a flaky test or update perf script -> review within 48 hours
- 1:1 check-ins: hiring manager (Day 3), people ops (Day 5)

Week 2-4 (Days 8-30)
- Rotation: shadow on-call/triage for 1 shift (lighter ops tasks only)
- Deliverable: Merge first non-trivial change (explain in PR the considerations for latency/cost)
- Documentation: update or create one internal doc that simplifies an onboarding pitfall (e.g., env var pitfalls)
- Feedback loop: 2-week checkpoint with hiring manager + mentor; update success criteria

30-90 (Growth & Impact)
- 30-day outcome: independent ownership of a small feature or critical bugfix; peer feedback collected
- 60-day outcome: leads a micro-project and drives an A/B or perf experiment
- 90-day outcome: measurable contribution to team metric (latency reduction, cost lowering, reliability)

Mentor pairing rota (practical rules):
- Primary mentor: same subteam, 4-6 weeks of weekly 1:1 + ad-hoc pairing.
- Secondary reviewer: cross-team reviewer who checks pull requests for integration/ops concerns for first 3 months.
- Mentor responsibilities checklist: onboarding doc walkthrough, triage shadow, first PR review within 48h, performance experiment demo at week 6.

Risk register (quick):
- Risk: Delayed access to internal GPU pools -> Mitigation: provide synthetic local benchmarks + quota escalation path (SRE oncall).
- Risk: Interview evidence inconsistent across loop -> Mitigation: use this rubric template and require 1-line evidence per interviewer before final packet.
- Risk: Remote hire not integrated with async docs -> Mitigation: schedule explicit async documentation hours and pair with doc-ownership task.

Offer & handoff checklist (post-accept):
- Confirm start date and timezone; block first-week meeting slots.
- Send equipment form to IT; cc hiring manager.
- Create onboarding PR in hr-playbooks repo that summarizes interview evidence -> link in new hire packet.

Practical templates (copy/paste anchors):
- Interview evidence line: DATE | INTERVIEWER | FOCUS | QUOTE (short) | SCORE 1-5 | FLAG(S) | NEXT STEP
- First-week PR template title: "onboarding: {name} - run example perf and notes"
- Mentor weekly note: "Week {n}: areas observed, 1 improvement, 1 wins, recommended next task"

Notes / outstanding questions (notes to self):
- Do we require a formalized take-home for infra roles? Pros: richer signal. Cons: delays pipeline. Propose pilot for 6 weeks.
- Need to align with SRE for guaranteed light oncall shadow windows. Ticket filed: SRE-ops-337 (pending).
- Quick wins: create a Google Sheet tracker for evidence logging that auto-generates a one-pager for hiring packets.

Action items (next steps):
- Maya: run pilot variant with encrypted take-home task for 3 infra hires by 2025-03-30.
- Ava: build the onboarding PR template in hr-playbooks repo before new hires next month.
- Liam: sync with SRE to formalize shadow oncall windows by 2025-03-15.

Appendix: example completed evidence entry (realistic but anonymized):
- 2025-02-18 | Sofia Martinez | Collaboration | "drove cross-team alignment on fallback routing via weekly sync" | 5 | -- | recommended: fast-track to offer

This file intentionally kept as an operational playbook (checklist + evidence). Feedback welcome — add comments in the Confluence draft or ping #people-ops on Slack for quick sync.
